title: AI Images
subtitle: Make and edit pictures in Gemini on purpose: memes, photo edits, logos, ads and study helpers. Use the same words real designers use.
bigIdea: Picture AI starts from random static (noise) and cleans it, step by step, into what your prompt describes. The clearer your design words are (subject, place, style, camera, light, shape), the more control you have. Great pictures come from good choices, not lucky prompts.
objectives: Explain how picture AI turns noise into a picture, and why the words you use change the result.
Write picture prompts with the Image Prompt Formula (Subject · Setting · Style · Camera · Light & color · Shape) using real camera words like close-up, from above and 16:9.
Edit pictures in Gemini by asking for changes (remove background, swap one thing, expand, sharpen), and label edits honestly.
Design your own brand look (logo, colors, fonts) and ads that put the biggest thing first and end with a clear call to action.
Make study helpers (flashcards, diagrams, picture notes) and check every AI fact and label.

vocabulary.definition: An AI that starts with random static and cleans it, step by step, into a picture.
vocabulary.analogy: Fog clearing slowly to show a picture behind it.
vocabulary.example: Gemini's picture maker (Nano Banana).

vocabulary.definition: Random fuzzy dots. Picture AI starts from noise.
vocabulary.analogy: TV static, or a foggy window.
vocabulary.example: Step 1 of every AI picture.

vocabulary.definition: Making a new picture from words you type.
vocabulary.analogy: Telling an artist on the phone what to draw.
vocabulary.example: 'A pixel-art fox astronaut.'

vocabulary.definition: Asking the AI to change a picture it already made, in the same chat.
vocabulary.analogy: Asking a hairdresser for 'a little shorter on the sides'.
vocabulary.example: 'Same picture, but make the sky purple.'

vocabulary.definition: How wide or tall a picture is.
vocabulary.analogy: A phone screen vs. a TV screen.
vocabulary.example: 1:1 square post, 9:16 phone story, 16:9 slide.

vocabulary.definition: Where things sit in the picture.
vocabulary.analogy: Moving furniture around a room.
vocabulary.example: The subject on the left, empty space for words on the right.

vocabulary.definition: Picture a 3 × 3 grid. Put the main thing on a line, or where two lines cross.
vocabulary.analogy: A tic-tac-toe board over your photo.
vocabulary.example: The horizon on the bottom line.

vocabulary.definition: How close the camera is, and where it looks from.
vocabulary.analogy: Standing far away vs. right up close.
vocabulary.example: Close-up, far away, from above, looking up.

vocabulary.definition: The art look of a picture.
vocabulary.analogy: The same song played as rock or as jazz.
vocabulary.example: Pixel art, watercolor, 3D clay, flat cartoon.

vocabulary.definition: Changing one part INSIDE a picture.
vocabulary.analogy: Sewing a patch on your jeans.
vocabulary.example: 'Take away the stain on the shoe.'

vocabulary.definition: Making a picture wider or taller. AI fills in the new edges.
vocabulary.analogy: Drawing what's outside a window frame.
vocabulary.example: Turn a square picture into a wide banner.

vocabulary.definition: Making a picture bigger and sharper with AI.
vocabulary.analogy: A magnifying glass that also adds detail.
vocabulary.example: Turn a small logo into a poster-size picture.

vocabulary.definition: A brand's symbol. It can be a name, a picture, or both.
vocabulary.analogy: The crest on a sports team's shirt.
vocabulary.example: An icon + name logo: a leaf drop next to the word 'Sip'.

vocabulary.definition: The colors, fonts, logo and style a brand always uses.
vocabulary.analogy: A school uniform for a company.
vocabulary.example: A brand board with 3 colors, 2 fonts and a logo.

vocabulary.definition: Making the most important thing the easiest to see.
vocabulary.analogy: Newspaper headlines are bigger than the story.
vocabulary.example: Big product picture → title → small details.

vocabulary.definition: Words that tell people what to do next.
vocabulary.analogy: A 'Push here' sign on a button.
vocabulary.example: 'Try it free', 'Order now'.

vocabulary.definition: A big difference between light and dark, or between colors, so things stand out.
vocabulary.analogy: White chalk on a dark board.
vocabulary.example: Yellow words on dark blue.

vocabulary.definition: A mark that shows a picture was made or changed by AI. Some are hidden, some you can see.
vocabulary.analogy: An artist's name signed on a painting.
vocabulary.example: Google's hidden SynthID mark, and our #MadeWithAI label.

vocabulary.definition: A funny picture with a few words that people share and change.
vocabulary.analogy: A joke pattern like 'knock knock'.
vocabulary.example: Two pictures: 'what I wanted' vs. 'what I got'.

vocabulary.definition: Learning with words AND pictures together.
vocabulary.analogy: Two roads to the same memory.
vocabulary.example: A flashcard with a word and a drawing.

gamification.questLine: A made-up company (the student picks it) hires the Guild to design its whole look: memes, product pictures, a logo, ads and study helpers for its buyers.
gamification.badge: 🎨 Pixel Forger: a finished Brand Kit that scores 3 or more on every rubric row.
gamification.boss: Brand Kit Showcase: logo + brand board + 1 social post + 1 poster + 1 study helper, all labeled as AI-made, then a 60-second pitch. 1-on-1: pitch to the teacher plus a guest.
sideQuests: Style Remix: make one picture in 5 art styles and name each one (+25 XP).
Glitch Fixer: find 3 AI glitches in your own pictures (extra fingers, mixed-up letters, odd shadows) and fix them with follow-up asks (+25 XP).
Make a comic for beginners: 'How picture AI works' (+25 XP).
Real vs. AI: take a real photo of a toy and make the same shot in Gemini. Which is better, and why? (+25 XP).

safety.teach: Gemini on the student's own account is the main tool. Before uploading a real photo, check it shows only objects or places, and nothing private (like an address on a letter).
Edit only objects, free public pictures or AI-made characters. Never classmates, teachers or famous people. Talk about it: how could an edited photo hurt someone?
No real brand logos, famous people or other people's characters in prompts. No 'in the style of [a living artist]'. Describe the look instead. Our brands are made up and our own.
Every picture gets a #MadeWithAI or 'AI-edited' label. Ads must not show fake results or fake reviews.
AI diagrams and flashcards can have wrong labels or mixed-up letters. Check every study helper against a textbook before sharing it.
Memes joke about moments, not people. No memes about classmates, groups or real people.

finalProject.title: Brand Kit for a Made-Up Company
finalProject.brief: Each student makes up a company (like water bottles that help the Earth, a dog-walking app, or a bakery for robots). Using Gemini (and Google Slides or Canva for layout), they make a whole Brand Kit and pitch it in 60 seconds. In a group, they pitch to the class. 1-on-1, they pitch to the teacher and a guest. The brand comes back in the Video and Website modules.
deliverables: Brand Brief (name, buyers, 3 personality words, mission sentence)
Logo (icon + name) and an icon-only version, tested at a tiny size
Brand board: 3 to 5 colors with codes, 2 fonts, logo, mood pictures
1 social post (1:1 or 9:16) with a title and a call to action
1 poster or ad (biggest first + call to action)
1 study helper for buyers (a how-to diagram or flashcards), fact-checked
Prompt Log with 3 or more tries for each piece, and AI labels

levels: Pieces don't match each other or the buyers
Everything matches and fits the buyers and personality words
Every choice (color, font, style) is explained with design words
Image Prompt Formula used, 3 or more tries per piece written down
Strong control: camera shots, shapes, follow-up edits, same character every time
No clear message or call to action
Biggest first, easy-to-read words, strong call to action
Honest and convincing, tested on someone and made better
Uses real brands or people, or no AI label
All pieces are your own and labeled, study helper fact-checked
Explains how you avoided unfair patterns, copying and tricky claims

finalProject.levelUp: Make a mascot for the brand that looks the same in 3 scenes, plus a moving sticker of it. That leads into the Video module!

support: Image Prompt Formula fill-in card with word lists (styles, camera shots, light).
Brand Brief with example answers. Pick from 6 starter company ideas.
Starter pages ready in Google Slides or Canva.
Group: Prompter and Art Director roles, swapping for each piece. 1-on-1: the student is the Art Director and you are the Prompter for one piece, then swap.
A smaller kit is OK: logo + 1 post + 1 study helper (can still earn the badge at level 3).
extension: Keep a mascot the same in many scenes using a character sheet and follow-up asks.
Write a mini brand rule book (do's and don'ts).
Make the same picture 3 times in Gemini with tiny prompt changes. Write what each word did.
Color play: test color pairs and check if words are easy to read with a free contrast checker.

carryForward: The company and Brand Kit become the client for Module 2 (launch video) and Module 3 (website + store).
